name: Graco Extend2Fit 3-in-1
price_note: Walmart list price (sold by Walmart.com); on sale $202.49 on 2026-10-04. gracobaby.com blocks automated checks. The 2-in-1 Extend2Fit is a cheaper sibling (Wirecutter top pick).

specs.child_range: RF harness 4–50 lb; FF harness 26.5–65 lb; highback booster 40–100 lb

recall_status: None found 2016–2026 for the 3-in-1. The older 2-in-1 Extend2Fit had a 2016 recline-label recall (16C-002, made Nov 27 2015–Jan 20 2016).
why: Ranked on evidence: independent crash results and lab agreement first, then recall record, proven features, usability. Three independent sources agree: CR crash 'Best', BabyGearLab crash 8.5 ('Best Value for Crash Test Analysis') and Wirecutter's top all-in-one pick; it also rear-faces to 50 lb at the lowest price here.
cautions: No belt lock-off; CR says newborn recline may need a rolled towel
Recline lever easy to confuse with the leg-extension panel (CR)
BabyGearLab data dated Sep 2025
sources: NHTSA recall flat file (2016–2026 child-seat campaigns)

name: Nuna RAVA Next
price_note: Nuna US list price for most colors; one color on sale at $525 and LoveShackFancy edition $600.

specs.child_range: RF 5–50 lb (LATCH to 35 lb), 18–49 in; FF 30–65 lb (LATCH to 40 lb), 34–49 in

recall_status: None found for RAVA Next. The original RAVA (made Jul 16 2016–Oct 25 2023) was recalled under 24C-002 for a harness adjuster that could loosen.
why: Ranked on evidence: independent crash results and lab agreement first, then recall record, proven features, usability. CR crash 'Best' and BabyGearLab crash 8.4 agree, with BabyGearLab's #3 overall score (80) and easy belt install (8.8); rear-faces to 50 lb, but costs about twice the top two.
cautions: CR ease of use 3/5; no rear-facing recline indicator (CR)
Width listed as 19–21 in (Nuna)
Check a used RAVA is a Next, not an original RAVA under recall 24C-002

name: Joie Saffron SI 4-in-1

specs.child_range: RF harness 4–40 lb, up to 43 in; FF harness 30–65 lb; booster up to 120 lb

recall_status: None found 2016–2026 (no Joie child-seat recall in the NHTSA file)
why: Ranked on evidence: independent crash results and lab agreement first, then recall record, proven features, usability. CR gives it its highest crash rating ('Best', CR Expert Pick for all-in-ones) and BabyGearLab's crash score of 8.3 is well above the 7.8 average of the seats it tested. It ranks below the RAVA Next because BabyGearLab found belt installation hard (5.0).

Rear-faces to 40 lb
